To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the complex structure of P.  vortex colony is generated by two morphotypes with distinct functions in colonization, (ii) the explorers are highly motile, hyperflagellated, antibiotic-tolerant and spearhead colony expansion, (iii) the explorers use a quorum-sensing system to coordinate their behaviour and (iv) the explorers have an increased resistance to antibiotics, which is due to the downregulation of ATP levels.
P. vectors uses two morphotypes to form complex colony structures and that the ‘explorers’, which spearhead colonial expansion, have a high level of motility and antibiotic resistance.
P. vorce swarming colonies contain two morphotypes, builders and explorers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a highly motilic and antibiotic resistant subpopulation of cells, the explorers, that spearhead the expansion of swarms of Paenibcillus vortex.
the identification and characterization of a subpopulation of cells that spearhead the expansion of P. vortex colony, and which is highly motile, hyperflagellated and refractory to antibiotics.
the identification of the highly motile and refractory to antibiotics subpopulation of Paenibaciullus vortex.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
P. vortex uses swarming and cell-to-cell signalling to form a modular colony.

the P. vorce explorers are characterized by a hypermotile phenotype, which enables them to spearhead colonial expansion and to translocate through antibiotic-containing areas, and this phenotype is achieved through the modulation of flagella expression and ATP levels.
the P. vortices colony is formed by two morphotypes with distinct functions in the colony formation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
P. vorce has a complex colony structure that allows it to adapt to the environment.
the P. vorce colony has two morphotypes: builders and explorers.
the complex structure and function of a P. vectors colony is generated by a coexistence and transition of two morphotypes – builders and explorers – with distinct roles in colony formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell-to-cell communication and cell differentiation allow P. vorce to form a complex, structured colony, which facilitates its dispersal and colonization on surfaces.
the explorers, with their increased antibiotic tolerance, may play a role in the dispersal of the colony in the presence of antibiotics and in the expansion of the colony into new habitats.
the explorers, with their high motility and antibiotic resistance, play an important role in the dispersal and survival of the colony.
